items.action: None, unless the app sets data-theme on <html> before startup and still wants the OS to drive the theme: set that attribute before startup only when the user has saved a choice.
items.appliesWhen: Apps calling provideDsTheme({ followSystem: true }) whose <html> already carries data-theme when the app starts, from index.html or a pre-bootstrap script. Apps without followSystem, or with no data-theme at startup, are unchanged.
items.pitfall: A data-theme hard-coded in index.html now pins the theme for every user, so the OS switch silently stops working.
items.verify: with followSystem on, an <html> that starts with data-theme keeps that value across an OS colour-scheme change, and one that starts without it follows the OS.

items.action: None, unless a group projects more avatars than max and all of them should stay visible: raise max to that count.
items.appliesWhen: ds-avatar-group elements projecting more ds-avatar children than max (default 4), or projecting more than max with no total. Groups projecting max or fewer avatars render as before.
items.verify: a group projecting more avatars than max shows max avatars followed by a +N chip whose N is the hidden count, or total - max when total is set.

items.action: Build after upgrading, and rename a member of yours the compiler reports as colliding.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class of yours that extends AvatarGroupComponent. Template users of ds-avatar-group need nothing; subclassing a DS component is unsupported.
items.pitfall: A redeclared private member collides as a public one does, and override cannot resolve it (TS2415); only a rename does.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS2415 or TS4114 against AvatarGroupComponent.

informational: --ds-topbar-crumb-text-color, --ds-topbar-crumb-hover-text-color, --ds-topbar-crumb-separator-icon-color, --ds-topbar-crumb-current-text-color, --ds-page-header-crumb-text-color and --ds-page-header-crumb-text-color-hover now recolour the projected ds-breadcrumbs, where they changed nothing; an app that set them sees those colours take effect.
ds-bar-chart draws a row with a negative value as an empty track labelled with that value, where it drew a bar of the absolute value labelled 0.

ds-button with routerLink or href, disabled and a disabledReason keeps a Tab stop (tabindex 0, role link) so the reason is announced; without disabledReason a disabled link-button still takes tabindex -1.
